title: Starship Flight 15 / Starlink Group 31-2 (OLP-2, Starbase)
t0_note: SpaceX Flight 15 page: 75-minute window opens 4:45 p.m. CT = 2026-11-13T22:45:00Z, pending regulatory approval. LL2 id 0f867f0c-5422-4d44-93b8-d7faaae7019b, status To Be Confirmed, window 22:45Z–00:00Z (checked 2026-11-11).

azimuth_deg.derived: great-circle bearing from the LL2 pad (25.99677N, 97.15799W) to the far-edge midpoint (20.6042N, 81.6500W) of NAVAREA IV 1080/26 Area A (Gulf of America / Yucatan Channel launch corridor, 132245Z-140040Z Nov and daily backups). Non-rotating i ~31.01 deg. MKJK A0455/26 (further downrange Jamaica FIR debris area) centroid bearing 107.40 deg / i~30.94. Geometric azimuth for 30.5 deg from this pad is 106.54 deg. Hazard-area azimuth kept (NOTAM-first). Source: https://space-notices.com/notice/nav-warning-NAVAREA%20IV%201080%2F26

payload_kg.note: FITTED within 20–80 t so the published 489 s ship ascent cutoff delivers the ASSUMED passively safe −40 × 275 km ellipse 1081 s before apogee. 26 Starlink V3 mass unpublished; result is NOT an estimate of the real stack.

insertion_alt_km.derived: Two-body equatorial-radius altitude on a −40 × 275 km ellipse, 1081 s before apogee (the published interval from Starship engine cutoff T+489 s to insertion start T+1570 s). Mid-arc, not perigee. See sma_km and fpa_deg.

apoapsis_alt_km.note: SpaceX: 'orbit the Earth at an altitude of ~275 km and complete approximately 14 orbits'. The ~275 km figure is the post-insertion orbital altitude. Apogee of the pre-insertion passively safe ellipse is set to the same 275 km so the 20 s insertion can circularize at that altitude.

fpa_deg.derived: Two-body flight-path angle 1081 s before apogee on the −40 × 275 km ellipse.

sma_km.derived: Absolute SMA of the −40 × 275 km passively safe stand-in (A=6378.137). Overrides the default (hp+ha)/2+R construction, which would be wrong because insertion_alt_km is a mid-arc altitude, not perigee.

target.altitude_reference: equatorial-radius (r - 6378.137 km) for SMA and the 162.59 km cutoff altitude target
target.note: SpaceX F15 official: the flight profile is designed with the opportunity to insert into a passively safe suborbital trajectory, then raise to orbital altitude (~275 km), 'similar to Starship’s first orbital mission'. SpaceX F14 official: after ascent the ship 'achieved its planned, passively safe suborbital trajectory', then 'reignited a single Raptor sea-level engine to perform an orbit insertion burn'. Pre-insertion perigee is unpublished; −40 km is a labelled stand-in in that passively-safe class (not a first-hand F15 element). The previous 180 × 275 km already-orbital target made a 20 s / 1×250 tf insertion ~2× too large in Δv.

header_notes: PRE-FLIGHT ILLUSTRATIVE. Starship Flight 15 / Starlink Group 31-2, 26 V3 sats, OLP-2 Starbase, T0 2026-11-13T22:45:00Z (Fri Nov 13 2:45 p.m. PST), 75-minute window, LL2 TBC pending regulatory approval. First attempt to catch both Super Heavy V3 and the ship at the launch site.

Ascent event times are SpaceX's published F15 timeline (MECO 139 s, hot-stage 141 s, ship cutoff 489 s). The 20 s orbital insertion burn (26:10–26:30) is a single sea-level Raptor 3 at 250 tf (F14 official analog: 'reignited a single Raptor sea-level engine'), flown open-loop for the published 20 s; payload deploy start 35:01, complete 1:17:40. Ship is then scheduled to fly ~14 orbits and attempt RTLS catch (deorbit T+21:35:57) — deorbit/catch are not in this file, which ends at deploy complete.

Ascent target is a passively safe suborbital ellipse (−40 × 275 km stand-in) at T+489 s, 1081 s before apogee, so the published insertion epoch is at first apogee. SpaceX F15 official text uses that architecture. 180 × 275 km (previous file) was the wrong energy class.

burns.name: Orbital insertion burn

t_ign_s.src: https://www.spacex.com/launches/starship-flight-15 Starship orbital insertion burn start T+00:26:10

duration_s.src: https://www.spacex.com/launches/starship-flight-15 shutdown T+00:26:30 (20 s). F14 official insertion was T+00:25:17–25:36 (19 s) on a single sea-level Raptor.

thrust_N.derived: Open-loop thrust that circularizes the post-coast state at the published insertion epoch. At T+1570 s the stage is at osculating −31.8 × 269.3 km, v=7.6534 km/s; circular speed at that radius is 7.7432 km/s (Δv 89.8 m/s). With m0=231,400.8 kg, Isp 350 s and the published 20 s, the rocket equation gives 1,028,650 N = 104.9 tf = 42.0% of the official 250 tf Raptor 3 sea-level rating. Labelled throttle of a single sea-level Raptor (F14 official analog), inside the commonly cited 40–100% range. Not a published F15 throttle setting.

isp_s.note: Sea-level Raptor vacuum Isp ~350 s (Musk, 9 Sep 2019); insertion is a single sea-level engine in near-vacuum.

burns.basis: Open-loop: published 20 s insertion on a single sea-level Raptor 3 (F14 official analog), throttled to 1,028,650 N (42% of 250 tf) so the burn supplies the 89.8 m/s needed to circularize the post-coast −31.8 × 269.3 km ellipse. Full 250 tf × 20 s would be ~200 m/s and would loft apogee. The ~6 km shortfall vs SpaceX’s ~275 km is J2/drag on the 18-minute coast from the −40 × 275 km ascent target.

deploy.src: SpaceX Flight 15 timeline: deploy start T+00:35:01, complete T+01:17:40
deploy.label: Starlink V3 deploy complete (26 sats)

notes: SpaceX F15 official: passively safe suborbital opportunity, then raise to ~275 km. Insertion is the published 20 s single-SL-Raptor burn with thrust solved to a 275 km perigee (labelled throttle). Residuals vs 275 km circular are reported, not hidden.

Deorbit burn T+21:35:57 and ship catch T+22:32:34 (SpaceX F15 timeline) are not modelled; file ends at deploy complete T+01:17:40. Leftover ship propellant after insertion stands in for those unpublished later burns.

fitted.method: scipy least_squares (TRF, bounded) vs published knots + target orbit

payload_kg.basis: 26 Starlink V3 satellites, mass unpublished by SpaceX. Fitted payload is a steering parameter, NOT an estimate of the real stack.
